topic: The febrile child: assessment, red flags and paediatric sepsis
scope: NICE NG143 on assessing fever in children under 5, including the traffic-light system and when to think of sepsis.

keyRecommendations.text: Think 'Could this be sepsis?' and use the NICE suspected-sepsis guideline if fever is accompanied by symptoms or signs of possible sepsis.
Assess the risk of serious illness with the traffic-light system.
Pneumonia red-flag signs include age-specific tachypnoea, crackles, nasal flaring, chest indrawing, cyanosis, and low oxygen saturation.

clinicalBottomLine: In a febrile child under 5, use the traffic-light assessment and ask whether this could be sepsis, referring to the sepsis guideline when suggestive signs are present.
notableCaveats: NG143 points to a separate sepsis guideline rather than reproducing a full paediatric sepsis bundle.

source.title: Fever in under 5s: assessment and initial management. NICE guideline NG143.
